hardening_changes.old_behavior: PVO-forward framing could suppress a source before a separate explicit explosion/impact statement was evaluated.
hardening_changes.new_behavior: A retained event statement with explicit explosion/impact evidence is evaluated normally even when the article also emphasizes PVO. PVO_ONLY remains non-positive when no separate explosion/impact evidence exists.
hardening_changes.generalizability_rationale: The same framing failure appeared in Slice 1 and can occur in any PVO-forward report.
anti_overfit_safeguards: exact locality, aerial context and episode-specific timing remain required

hardening_changes.old_behavior: After generic retrieval failed, the fallback was limited to a fixed trusted-domain universe.
hardening_changes.new_behavior: For unresolved episodes, add an indexed local/regional-news fallback parameterized by target city, local date, alert-hour envelope, explosion/impact vocabulary and aerial-war vocabulary. Domain membership only widens retrieval and never supplies evidence.
hardening_changes.generalizability_rationale: Unique contemporaneous reporting can appear on indexable local outlets not represented in a previous calibration domain list.
anti_overfit_safeguards: full-body evidence must pass unchanged classification guardrails

hardening_changes.old_behavior: Event-hour retrieval could miss later same-day or D+1 publications that explicitly describe an earlier target event.
hardening_changes.new_behavior: For unresolved episodes, search the target local event date plus a D+1 publication window. Attribution still requires body-level event date/time or unambiguous chronology; publication/update time is never used as event time.
hardening_changes.generalizability_rationale: Air-attack reporting is often updated or published retrospectively while preserving explicit earlier event timing.
anti_overfit_safeguards: publication/update lag cannot create a positive in a later alert

hardening_changes.old_behavior: A long live page could be found without retaining the relevant timestamped entry as an independent event statement.
hardening_changes.new_behavior: Scan the full available live-feed body and segment timestamped entries. Evaluate each entry, or only tightly compatible neighboring entries in the same attack sequence, for locality, explosion/impact, aerial context and target-episode timing.
hardening_changes.generalizability_rationale: Live chronologies commonly contain many localities and attacks under one page publication timestamp.
anti_overfit_safeguards: no locality transfer between unrelated entries
neighbor composition only within one compatible sequence
page publication time is not event time

hardening_changes.old_behavior: Minute-level event evidence could be called strict when the alert began partway through the same minute.
hardening_changes.new_behavior: When event timing is only minute-granular and alert start is second-resolved inside that minute, strict requires independent ordering evidence that the event occurred after alert start or an unambiguous semantic after/during relation. Otherwise keep the event sensitivity-positive/boundary-ambiguous.
hardening_changes.generalizability_rationale: This prevents invented second-level precision at any alert boundary.
anti_overfit_safeguards: historical verdict is not a runtime signal
explicit unambiguous ordering evidence can still establish strictness

unchanged_guardrails: publication time is not event time
headline context does not override qualifying body evidence
a headline about another locality does not block a separate Zaporizhzhia body event
cross-source composition only for a compatible event sequence
publication/update lag cannot create a positive in a later alert episode
